subject: Plotting unsmoothed covariate vs fitted values

messages.author: 863a0481c01d0ecd
messages.subject: Plotting unsmoothed covariate vs fitted values
parts:
Dear INLA people,

I have fitted a model with the following specifications in INLA
formula=y~f(inla.group(x, n=100), model rw2) + spatial + temporal effects.

from the model outputs, I am able to plot linear predictor vs fitted values and x vs the mean and sd of the smooth term. However I haven't been able to find a way to plot x vs. fitted values which would be very illustrative to interpret the model. Is there any way to do that (hopefully without re-running the model)?

Thanks for your advice,

Victor.

r$summary.{fixed,random,fitted.values, etc...}

should give you access to the summary statistics and you can plot what
you want ;-)

Thank you Havard. The problem is that I am getting way less values for random effects and the smooth term than for the linear predictor and the fitted values (93 vs 3,300 in the best case). I guess that has to do with the grouping of the covariate which was necessary in order to avoid INLA to crash. Therefore I cannot find 1 to 1 correspondence between x and the fitted values. Is there a way to link them?

Thanks,

Victor.

and then plot

f(x.true) againsta the fitted values.
